### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class), inheritsElevation (symbol, a const object of class ScopedContext))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **29** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `91e761d521fd6dc1a61c94edef74e712b927be7c` — the merge of head `d0489d5e4513eec99d83dc16dab8737f61bae5f5` into base `cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 91e761d521fd6dc1a61c94edef74e712b927be7c && git checkout 91e761d521fd6dc1a61c94edef74e712b927be7c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671 d0489d5e4513eec99d83dc16dab8737f61bae5f5 && git checkout -B drift-repro cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671 && git merge --no-ff d0489d5e4513eec99d83dc16dab8737f61bae5f5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d0489d5e4513eec99d83dc16dab8737f61bae5f5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-binder.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-run-as.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-run-as.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/flow-system-identity-write-refusal.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-automation-identity-write-refusal.integration.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (the second `wrapDeclarativeHook` door, the audit builtins), packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts (`ql.bindHooks`, `wrapHandler`), packages/runtime/src/stored-metadata-reader-seam.ts (`deriveThroughSeam`), packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts (`buildSandboxApiSource`, the action-body factory), packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts (the READ and WRITE method lists), packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`buildActionExecutionContext`, unchanged), packages/core/src/security/app-automation-elevation.ts (unchanged), packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts (`HookContext.ql`, `HookContext.api`), AGENTS.md (the semver rule); the prose faces (content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx, .changeset/25653-app-hook-inherited-elevation-identity-write-refusal.md) read with them. No path is a remainder.

### ① Derived judgments

Read on the net diff `origin/main...origin/pr-25982` (five commits: the red pin `cb6bb395a2` alone, the fix `4a7683e2a3`, then docs and changeset `ec46d1e142`, objectql pins `1a96cdaa6e`, plugin-security pin `d0489d5e45`), the cited code on the head, card #25653 (body and all eight comments, with the slice-1 contract review 6408962867 on PR #25954 that the claim's `Thread-read` names), the PR body and file list, and the check-runs on the head.

**CI state at review time.** 47 check-runs on `d0489d5e`: 35 concluded `success` (TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 of 8, Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates (which holds `check:system-context-census`), Lint · CI, release & engine gates, the three scoped lints, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, the three claim guards, Auto Label, Check PR Size, filter), 11 `skipped` (UI matrix stubs and opt-in harnesses), and ONE still `in_progress`: Test Core (4/8). So every typecheck, lint, changeset and census family has concluded green on the head; one test shard has not. This record judges the diff and the concluded gates; the dev's local counts (objectql 8734, plugin-security 4683, runtime 7232, core 2763 passed; runtime pin 100/100; two ablations each turning exactly its own rows red) are the dev's claim, not a gate verdict.

**Accept-set change: three app-authored elevations are now refused.** The door is unchanged: the data middleware's one call to `assertFlowSystemIdentityWriteAllowed` ahead of the `isSystem` bypass, and the predicate `elevationSource` (`isSystem` AND (`flowRunId` OR the core mark)) is byte-identical to slice 1. What moves is who carries the mark. New producers, each read on the head: (1) `ScopedContext[APP_AUTHORED_HOOK_API]()` marks `'hook'` on a context that is `isSystem` with no `flowRunId` and no mark of its own — the hook inherited a platform system write's elevation; a run's context stays the run's, a marked context keeps its mark, a user's context is not elevated and gets none; (2) `ScopedContext.sudo()` marks `'hook'` when the api's private `appAuthored` flag is set and the elevated copy carries no mark yet, and the flag rides every child the new `derive()` helper builds (`transaction` joined and owned, `beginTransaction`, `withRunAs` both arms, the `'user'` grant seeding); (3) `ObjectRepository.execute()` marks its `{ ...this.context, isSystem: true }` elevation `'action'`, the same mark `buildActionExecutionContext` gives the REST and MCP doors, and hands that context to both `executionContext` and the `api` it builds for the handler. Refused set: the six governed verbs on exactly `sys_user_position`, `sys_user_permission_set`, `sys_invitation`, `sys_member` from any of those contexts; reads of the four and writes to every other object stay admitted (pinned: the inheriting hook still updates `qa_note`). RIGHT, and the shape the slice-1 ruling (③ item 3) asked for: one predicate, one module, no new error code.

**The discriminator: a hook is app-authored when the hook binder bound it.** `bindHooksToEngine` wraps every hook it binds with `appAuthored: true` (a constant in the binder's own call, not a value read from the hook) and registers it with `meta: hook`. `ObjectQL.registerHook` stores `meta` on the entry; `triggerHooks` and `dispatchUnscopedMultiWriteHooks` skip an entry under `skipAutomations` exactly when `entry.meta` is set, and `opensAfterAbortUnit` reads `entry.meta` the same way. So "bound through the binder" and "the set `skipAutomations` keys on" are one set by construction, as the PR body says. Platform hooks are registered in code with no `meta`: the audit, approvals, auth, email and security plugins' `engine.registerHook(...)` calls carry `object`, `priority`, `packageId` and nothing else. The one other `wrapDeclarativeHook` caller on the head, `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` (the audit builtins), passes no `appAuthored` and registers with no `meta`: the platform wrap the PR body describes, unchanged. The runtime's app artifacts reach the binder through `ql.bindHooks` (`app-artifact-handlers.ts`), which is the engine's own proxy to `bindHooksToEngine`; stack and package `hooks:` go the same way. One door holds. RIGHT.

**Platform code keeps its writes.** `ScopedContext.appAuthored` defaults to `false`, and only `[APP_AUTHORED_HOOK_API]()` ever sets it `true`; `buildHookApi`, `createContext`, `ObjectRepository.execute()`'s own `new ScopedContext(...)` and every other construction leave it `false`, so their `sudo()` is the old `{ ...ctx, isSystem: true }` with no mark. Bare `{ isSystem: true }` writers carry neither a run nor a mark. Pinned end to end on the real stack: a hook registered in code writes each of the four from its inherited system context, from its `sudo()`, and through the declarative wrapper with no binding (`by_inherit`, `by_sudo`, `by_wrapped` all land); the objectql pin asserts a platform wrap hands the api through by reference (`toBe`) and marks neither path. RIGHT (card condition 2's pin, condition 4's fourth pin).

**The discriminator cannot be spoofed by app-authored metadata.** Judged in words. The flag is an argument the binder itself passes, so nothing an author writes in a hook reaches it; `hookRunAs` admits only the three declared values, and each keeps the provenance: `'inherit'` derives through the symbol method and marks an inherited elevation; `'user'` derives on the app-authored base and `derive()` keeps the flag, so its `sudo()` marks; `'system'` is marked directly; `'user'` with no triggering user yields `UnscopedHookApi`, which has `object` and `transaction` only, both refusing, and no `sudo`. The wrapper replaces `ctx.api` before the handler runs and keeps the original only in its own closure for the restore, so neither a handler nor a body sees the pre-derivation api; a fire-and-forget hook runs on a detached copy whenever an api was installed, so the synchronous restore cannot hand it back. A sandboxed body gets only `ctx.api` built from `engineCtx.api` (the derived one), with the fixed READ and WRITE lists plus `transaction`, and arguments cross as JSON, which cannot spell either symbol. The runtime's stored-metadata seam forwards `sudo`, `withRunAs`, `transaction` and `beginTransaction` by calling the wrapped api's own method and wrapping what it returns, so a seam over a marked api derives marked children and never rebuilds a context. The mark only ever narrows (its sole reader refuses and admits nothing). RIGHT.

**Slice-1 behaviour is unchanged.** `elevationSource` is untouched; `'flow'` still wins whenever `flowRunId` is set, so the system-flow refusal text stays byte-identical; `withRunAs('system')` still marks `'hook'` (now through `derive()`, same envelope); `buildActionExecutionContext` and the core module did not change; the `createContext` carry is still the one parse site (`engine.ts:22721`). The hook arm's SUBJECT and ASSIGNMENT_PRESCRIPTION strings widened to name the three ways a hook is elevated; the flow and action strings and MEMBERSHIP_PRESCRIPTION are unchanged, and slice 1's runtime `expectRefused` regexes still match the widened text. RIGHT.

**No fixture was loosened.** The plugin-security message pin follows the new wording exactly (a tighter regex, not a wider one). The objectql published-face pin moves from one unexported symbol-keyed member to two and adds an explicit assertion that `APP_AUTHORED_HOOK_API` is not exported from the package entry: a deliberate, honest update. The runtime integration file is additive apart from one import; slice 1's fifty cases and its CONTROL blocks are untouched. The new pin was committed red first (`cb6bb395a2` carries the test file alone). RIGHT.

**Each new path on each of the four objects, with code and prescription.** Inherited elevation: body and handler surfaces, four objects, insert, update and delete, each checked for `PERMISSION_DENIED`, 403, the hook subject and the per-object prescription, the store unchanged and the triggering write aborted (24 cases). `sudo()`: four objects by three verbs under a user's write, plus inside `ctx.api.transaction` and under `runAs: 'user'` (13). `execute()`: insert on each of the four (4). Controls: the inheriting hook still writes another object; under a user's write the ordinary gates refuse the plain member and the elevation refusal does not (`not.toMatch(/governed identity writes/)`); the code-registered hook family lands (9). `transfer`, `restore` and `purge` have no engine verb and stay covered at the predicate in plugin-security. RIGHT (card condition 4, first and second pins).

**Routes that remain unmarked, by the ruling's placement.** (a) `ObjectQL.executeAction` called directly by host code hands the handler whatever context the caller built (the report's first finding). (b) `HookContext.ql` hands an in-process handler the engine itself, whose doors take a caller-supplied context; a context built there is the host's own, unmarked, and is admitted exactly as platform code's is. The sandbox context does not carry `ql`. Both are host code constructing its own system context, the class slice 1 placed outside the ruled sites; neither is a defect of this diff. (c) `APP_AUTHORED_HOOK_API` is a module-local `Symbol()`, not `Symbol.for`, the same posture as `SEED_USER_GRANTS`: a `bindHooksToEngine` imported from a different build than the engine's would make `deriveAppAuthoredHookApi` return the api as is, which here fails open to an unmarked api rather than to a narrower one. The runtime's door is `ql.bindHooks` on the instance, which cannot mismatch, and the dual-build case has no caller on the head. Noted; non-blocking.

**Docs census row 1b** now names the inherited elevation, `sudo()` and `execute()` as producers and anchors `engine.ts#inheritsElevation`, which resolves to the `const inheritsElevation` declaration inside `[APP_AUTHORED_HOOK_API]()`, the one new `isSystem` read; `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (the census gate) concluded `success`. RIGHT.

**Nothing shipped starts being refused.** On the head, no caller of `ObjectRepository.execute()` exists in `packages/`, `apps/` or `examples/` (every `.execute(` hit is a driver, raw-SQL or flow-engine method); slice 1's census of the four objects in app hooks and HotCRM stands, and this slice adds no object to the refused set. The hooks-calling-`sudo()` half of the census is the dev's claim.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset `.changeset/25653-app-hook-inherited-elevation-identity-write-refusal.md` bumps `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` at `patch`: exactly the two packages the diff moves outside tests and prose (runtime changed a test file only; core did not change). RIGHT.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing: an app-authored hook's inherited or sudo() elevation, and an action reached through ObjectRepository.execute(), are refused the four identity objects at run time, as a runAs: 'system' hook already is)` is byte-identical between the PR body and the changeset, and `Metadata-protocol: none` is on both. The claim 6409338002 carries the seat's shorthand of the same arm. The arm is right: a served-set narrowing (a write once admitted is now refused), BREAKING by rule; `none` is right because nothing an author can write changes at save time (the save-time refusal and its ADR-0087 D3 entry stay with the `domain:spec` half, pointer on #6017).
- Carriers: the PR title is `fix(security)!:`; the changeset carries the BREAKING banner naming the audience (an app-authored hook that writes the four while elevated, census none) and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, in the gate's vocabulary; no authorable key is removed or renamed, so there is no migration to carry. `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded `success`.
- Level: by AGENTS.md "the level follows the kind alone ... `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". `patch` with the banner and the disposition is exactly that. The face: no governed-surface path is in the file list; the `(narrowing)` arm decides, so the review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the narrowing face.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report: comment 6411228574 on #25653; `status: done`, `premise_still_valid: true`, `open_questions: []`.

1. **The slice-1 escalation (6408962867 ③ item 3).** It asked that the inherited-elevation finding, the `execute()` third-caller note and the in-process `sudo()` route be filed as a card or put to the maintainer before the card closes. The claim's `Ruling-ref` records the maintainer's answer (a security finding is dispatched for a fix directly, no new card, no advisory), and this slice closes all three named routes. Consistent; the escalation is discharged.
2. **Report finding 1: `ObjectQL.executeAction` called directly by host code.** Confirmed by reading: `executeAction` looks the handler up and calls it with the context it was given. Only host code reaches it; the sandbox exposes no `execute`. Accepted as outside the ruled sites, with `HookContext.ql` added to the same class in ①. Carrier stays the seat; nothing blocks.
3. **Report finding 2: a platform hook nested under an app-authored hook's marked context is refused too.** Confirmed by construction: `buildHookApi(opCtx.context)` wraps the nested write's own context, and the mark rides that spread exactly as `flowRunId` does, the posture slice 1 accepted for `runAs: 'system'` hooks. Census found no platform hook writing the four through its inherited api. Accepted.
4. **Claimed surface and deviations.** The claim lists slice 1's surface plus "the objectql hook derivation"; `hook-binder.ts`, `hook-wrappers.ts` and `hook-run-as.ts` are that derivation, and `ObjectRepository.execute()` is the measurement the order asked for and the PR body names in Acceptance notes. No `packages/spec/**` touched, no new error code, the predicate unchanged, `sudo()` on platform code byte-identical. The dev's "tree identical to `7d29c9ab`" cannot be checked here (that commit is not on the fetched ref); it is the dev's claim and does not matter to the verdict, which is on the head. The runtime and core suites ran at the fix commit `4a7683e2`: verified that only two test files, the docs page and the changeset changed between it and the head.
5. **Slice-1 ③ item 1 (symbol vs declared field).** Not reopened by the report. This slice adds a second, objectql-private symbol with the same posture; the honest cost named in slice 1 (a future producer that rebuilds a context by parse or key-pick drops the mark fail-open) now also covers a derivation reached through the wrong build (① item c). Still the spec half's question; non-blocking.
6. **Slice-1 ③ item 4 disclosure gap.** This changeset's audience line names app-authored hooks and not a host-code action handler dispatched by an action door; the gap carried from slice 1 stays open for the spec half or a follow-up. Non-blocking.
7. **No reproduction.** The PR body's "Measured before any code" names which doors an in-process handler can reach, in the card's own words; it gives no steps, no payload and no body text. The report is the same. The test file is the ruled pin. Neither carries a reproduction, so there is no FAIL reason here.
8. **Gates not yet concluded.** Test Core (4/8) was `in_progress` when this record was rendered. The verdict is on the diff and the concluded gates; the owning seat does not queue until every check is green, and a red in that shard reopens this record on the same head.
9. **Remainder.** `Part of #25653` (the Part-of guard concluded `success`); the card stays open for the save-time refusal in `domain:spec`. Consistent with the claim and with slice 1.
